comments.author: Iso Tester
comments.body:
PASS 1 review (A1 — anti-slop / over-engineering / NIH) for the "Move .bridge_state/ + reconciler lock files off the shared tickets branch" follow-up plan.

AFFIRMATIONS (criteria this plan passes under A1):
- YAGNI / no new abstraction: this is a net *removal* plan (gitignore root files, delete the WU-3 `.gitattributes merge=ours`, simplify the push.py stash→merge→pop dance). It introduces no new class, dependency, or config key, so Rule-of-Three and premature-abstraction do not apply. Confirmed in src/rebar/_store/push.py (the `_DIRTY_WD` stash dance at lines 158-180 is exactly what "can be simplified once they leave the branch" refers to) and src/rebar/_commands/init.py (`_GITATTRIBUTES`/`_commit_gitattributes`/`_ensure_merge_ours_driver` are the WU-3 surface AC-3 proposes to retire).
- No NIH / golden-hammer / resume-driven / premature-optimization: the plan reuses git's native gitignore + the existing union-merge machinery rather than building a new mechanism; AC-2's "regression test" targets the existing union path. No trendy tech, no speculative optimization.
- Not config-surface proliferation: removing `merge=ours` *reduces* the .gitattributes/merge-driver config surface rather than adding to it.

Net: clean on the over-engineering axis — if anything it deletes machinery. The one A1-adjacent caveat is below (it is about an *under-specified replacement* that risks an over-built redesign, not about the removal itself).

FINDING (A1 — guard the deferred "coordination redesign" against re-building what git/the existing reconciler already give you):
- [ ] Before the redesign pass, scope the replacement coordination against existing mechanisms so it does not reinvent locking that the codebase already has. Grounding: AC-1 says coordination must be "preserved or redesigned" and Scope/risk says the reconciler "coordinates cross-clone partly VIA these shared-branch files." Concretely, `.bridge_state/bindings.json` is read cross-clone today via `git show tickets:...bindings.json` (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py:77,110; resolver.py:50) and the lock/gate files are read via `git show tickets:<file>` (_advisory_lock.py:172-214, check_pass_lock/check_phase_gate). Once these leave the branch there is no shared medium for that read — and rebar already owns several coordination primitives (the flock WRITE_LOCK_NAME / 30s mkdir MKDIR_LOCK_NAME in init.py; the rebase_retry + CAS serialization in _advisory_lock.py:448-586). The redesign should pick the smallest extension of one of these, not a bespoke new IPC/state channel — call that out explicitly so the follow-up's design pass is bounded.
  evidence: AC-1 ("coordination preserved or redesigned"); Scope/risk ("coordinates cross-clone partly VIA these shared-branch files"); binding_store.py:110 `git show tickets:.tickets-tracker/.bridge_state/bindings.json`; _advisory_lock.py `_git_show_tickets_file` (reads lock/gate off the branch); existing primitives WRITE_LOCK_NAME/MKDIR_LOCK_NAME (init.py:29) and rebase_retry/CAS (_advisory_lock.py).
  suggested_fix: In Scope/risk (or a new "Replacement coordination" note), name the candidate substrate for each moved concern — bindings cache vs. pass-lock vs. phase-gate — and state which existing primitive (flock write-lock, mkdir init-lock, rebase_retry/CAS) it extends, so the design pass cannot drift into a new bespoke coordination layer.

SCOPING NOTE (not an A1 finding; flagging for the author's other passes since it bounds the A1 surface): the plan's What/Files/AC name only `.bridge_state/bindings.json`, but `.bridge_state/` on disk also holds snapshots/, mapping.json, health/, manifests/, bridge_alerts/, prev_snapshot.json (see resolver.py:50, binding_store.py, and the reconciler apply/fetch/health writers). Most of those are pass-local working-tree artifacts, not committed cross-clone state — only bindings(-retired).json is committed (reconcile.py:237). Worth confirming the gitignore targets exactly the committed subset so the move neither strands a committed file nor over-gitignores a path some clone still expects on the branch. (Routing this to the correctness/coherence pass; A1 itself is clean.)

comments.author: Iso Tester
comments.body:
PASS-1 review note (T1 — prior-art / novel-architecture justification) for the follow-up plan "Move .bridge_state/ + reconciler lock files off the shared tickets branch". Recording for traceability; the structured finding follows in the review payload.

FINDING (T1a/T1b — prior art for the replacement cross-clone coordination):
- [ ] Before committing to moving the reconciler lock/gate (and `.bridge_state`) off the shared `tickets` branch, the plan should survey prior art for how the *replacement* cross-clone coordination will work — and justify the novel mechanism vs the established shared-branch approach it removes.

Grounding/evidence:
- The plan's own "Scope / risk" states: "The reconciler currently coordinates cross-clone partly VIA these shared-branch files; moving them off-branch changes that coordination and needs its own design pass." That is the load-bearing novelty: today the SHARED BRANCH itself is the coordination medium — `_advisory_lock.py` reads lock/gate via `git show tickets:<file>` (check_pass_lock / check_phase_gate, lines 222-408) and writes them as CAS-advanced commits on the tickets ref (`_commit_in_detached_tickets_worktree`, lines 491-586). A clone with no checkout of the branch can still observe the lock. Moving these off-branch removes that cross-clone visibility channel and requires a new one.
- ABSENCE: the plan names the three files to touch but does not identify what the off-branch coordination becomes (local-only? a different ref? a side channel?) nor cite prior art for it. This matters because a tickets-branch tool with NO shared-branch coordination state is a distinctly different distributed-coordination posture than peer tools — and the bar here is set high by THIS epic (97e7), whose own "Prior art" section surveyed git-bug, git-appraise, git-issue, and jujutsu with verifiable references before adopting union recovery. The follow-up should meet that same bar for the coordination replacement (e.g., how do git-bug / jujutsu / git-appraise coordinate concurrent writers across clones without a shared mutable coordination file?).
- AC line "reconciler coordination preserved or redesigned" currently under-specifies the redesign; a prior-art pass would let the author choose "preserved" vs "redesigned" deliberately rather than defer it.

AFFIRMATIONS (T1 PASS — no finding):
- The core "every path becomes append-only-disjoint ⇒ union merge can never wedge" claim reuses the ALREADY-ESTABLISHED union-merge recovery pattern in src/rebar/_store/sync.py (`_union_merge`, _do_reconverge) — a well-trodden, in-repo approach, not a novel architecture. No prior-art search is owed for that half.
- No unverified external-capability assertion ("library supports X") is present; the git-merge/union mechanics it relies on are already exercised by the parent epic's WU-2/WU-3.

compiled_state.description:
# P1.4 (rev) — Bounded git growth via stock gc + non-destructive (union) recovery

> Supersedes `seek-algae-reign` (a240-d692-a86f-411c). The original epic proposed a
> bespoke operator `rebar gc` with hand-tuned reflog/prune windows to protect a
> reflog-only recovery net. Critical evaluation + 7 git experiments + two Opus
> reviews (principal-engineer + peer-comparison) showed that design is an outlier:
> no comparable tool builds it, and it treats a symptom (a recovery path that
> orphans commits into the reflog) instead of the cause. This epic implements the
> peer-aligned design instead. Full design trail: session_log (see relates_to).

## Context (problem + why the rewrite)

Every ticket mutation is a committed file on the orphan `tickets` branch. The write
path forces `gc.auto=0` (`_store/event_append.py:74-84 _ensure_gc_auto_zero`, also
`compact.py:61`, `txn.py:217/413`, `init.py:182`) for ONE reason: to keep git's
reflog alive, because `_store/sync.py` `_do_reconverge` does
`git reset --hard origin/tickets` in the "unrelated histories" path (~71-85), which
**orphans local-only commits** and relies on the reflog to recover them (the
warning at `sync.py:81` literally says "recoverable: git reflog"). No durable ref
is saved before the reset. Cost: unbounded loose-object/pack growth with no safe
reclaim, and a recovery net that depends on an ephemeral, gc-governed structure
the operator cannot see.

## Validated facts (our experiments — see session_log)

- Reachable commits survive even `git gc --prune=now`; only `reset --hard` orphans
  + reflog-expiry can lose data (EXP-A/B).
- On the append-only branch `git gc` is ~96% repack/delta (2.5M -> 104K, 600 objects
  intact) and `--prune` reclaims ~nothing; "deleted"/compacted blobs stay reachable
  from history so `--compact-first` reclaims nothing for gc (EXP-E/G).
- `git gc` produces cruft packs by default on git >= 2.41 (EXP-F).
- A durable ref makes an orphaned commit survive a FULL reflog wipe + `gc --prune=now`
  (EXP-H) — i.e. reachability, not the reflog, is the durable guarantee.

## Prior art (verifiable references — the patterns we follow)

- **git-bug** — leaves `gc.auto` on, ships NO gc command, recovers by DAG **union
  merge (fast-forward-only, both parents kept), never `reset --hard`**; batches many
  ops into one blob/commit (operationPack):
  https://github.com/git-bug/git-bug/blob/master/entity/dag/entity_actions.go ,
  https://github.com/git-bug/git-bug/blob/master/entity/dag/operation_pack.go
- **git-appraise** — git-notes unioned via `cat_sort_uniq` (never drops); before its
  one rewrite path it **archives the old head to a ref "to keep history from being
  garbage collected"** (ref-reachability, not reflog):
  https://github.com/google/git-appraise/blob/master/repository/git.go ,
  https://github.com/google/git-appraise/blob/master/review/review.go
- **git-issue** — one-commit-per-change, stock gc, no bespoke maintenance:
  https://github.com/dspinellis/git-issue
- **jujutsu (jj)** — recovery net is the op log materialized as real `refs/jj/keep/`
  refs; gc (`jj util gc`) is safe because it only collects objects unreachable from
  retained refs => "gc reachability == recovery guarantee" co-design:
  https://docs.jj-vcs.dev/latest/operation-log/ ,
  https://docs.jj-vcs.dev/latest/technical/architecture/
- **git itself** — `gc.auto` default (6700 loose) is the normal posture; cruft packs
  default since 2.37/2.41; `--prune=now` risks corruption under concurrent writers;
  `git maintenance` is the scale-up scheduler (disabling gc.auto WITHOUT out-of-band
  maintenance is the anti-pattern, cf. Scalar/GitLab):
  https://git-scm.com/docs/git-gc , https://git-scm.com/docs/git-maintenance ,
  https://github.blog/open-source/git/highlights-from-git-2-37/ ,
  https://devblogs.microsoft.com/devops/introducing-scalar/

## Design + the safety invariant

Adopt the universal peer pattern: **trust stock `git gc`, and make recovery
non-destructive so the reflog is never load-bearing.**

> INVARIANT: after union recovery, every commit rebar cares about is ref-reachable;
> therefore stock `git gc` is safe by construction — it only ever collects truly
> unreachable objects.

This is jj's co-design lesson achieved for free: if commits are never orphaned,
gc has nothing unsafe to collect.

## Implementation plan (work units)

- **WU-1 Re-enable stock gc.** Delete `_ensure_gc_auto_zero` (`event_append.py:74-84`)
  + its call (`:124`); drop the four `git config gc.auto 0` writes (`txn.py:217`,
  `txn.py:413`, `compact.py:61`, `init.py:182`). Set `gc.autoDetach=true` explicitly
  at init so a forked background gc never serializes a foreground write. Migration:
  idempotent `git config --unset gc.auto || true` at init/fsck.
- **WU-2 Union, don't discard.** Replace the `reset --hard origin/tickets` in
  `sync.py` Path 1 (unrelated histories) with
  `git merge --allow-unrelated-histories origin/tickets --no-edit`, **reusing the
  existing diverged-Path-3 conflict -> `merge --abort` -> keep-local -> hint
  handling** (extend proven code, do not invent). Keep `reset --hard` only for the
  ff-adopt path (discards nothing).
- **WU-3 Conflict policy for mutable shared root files.** uuid-named ticket dirs
  never collide, but `.bridge_state/bindings.json` and the reconciler lock/gate
  files are rewritten per pass and would conflict. Add a tickets-branch
  `.gitattributes` with `merge=ours` for `.bridge_state/*` and `.reconciler-*`
  (the loser is a derived cache the reconciler rebuilds next pass — never ticket
  events). `merge=union` is WRONG (line-unions JSON into invalid JSON). NOTE:
  push.py already handles these conflicts today, so this only formalizes it.
- **WU-4 Docs + invariant.** Rewrite `docs/concurrency.md:165-196` and the `sync.py`
  module docstring (both assert the old reset+reflog design). State the safety
  invariant; note `git maintenance run` as the scale-up posture and that git's own
  30d-unreachable reflog window remains as a free backstop we no longer depend on.

## What this supersedes / drops from the old epic

- DROP the bespoke `rebar gc` command, `reflog expire --expire=<14d>`, the 14-day
  window rationale, `--compact-first` (reclaims nothing — EXP-G), and the
  `check_no_rebase_in_progress`-as-gc-guard (recovery is `reset --hard`, atomic, no
  marker — the guard cannot see it). None of this machinery exists in `src/` yet;
  this epic ensures it never gets built.

- [ ] Unrelated-history sync MERGES (never discards) local tickets; two clones each
